name: Melanotan I
route: Gray-market injections under the skin; the approved form is a clinician-placed implant
status: Not approved for tanning; the same molecule is FDA-approved only as Scenesse (afamelanotide) for a rare light-sensitivity disease
mechanism: Copies the hormone alpha-MSH at the MC1R receptor on pigment cells, boosting dark eumelanin to produce a tan without sun exposure

article.summary: Melanotan I is the research name for afamelanotide, a synthetic tanning hormone. It is sold online as an unapproved injection; the only approved form is an implant for a rare disease.
article.takeaway: Melanotan I is a lab-made version of alpha-MSH, the hormone that triggers tanning, developed at the University of Arizona in the 1980s. Small randomized trials showed injections darken skin without sun, and in fair-skinned volunteers it cut some markers of sunburn damage.[^1][^2] The molecule was later developed as **afamelanotide**, now an FDA-approved implant for erythropoietic protoporphyria.[^3] Powders sold online as "Melanotan 1" are a different matter: unregulated, of unknown purity and dose, and used without medical oversight.[^4]
glance: Not approved for tanning; approved only as Scenesse for EPP
Small randomized tanning trials in healthy volunteers; approved-drug trials in EPP
Unknown product quality, nausea, darkening and changing moles

blocks.text: Melanotan I is a 13-amino-acid copy of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone with two substitutions (norleucine at position 4 and a mirror-image phenylalanine at position 7) that make it more potent and longer-lasting than the natural hormone. It binds the melanocortin-1 receptor on melanocytes, which then produce more eumelanin, the brown-black pigment that absorbs light.[^5]

It is more focused on pigment than its cyclic cousin [Melanotan II](/peptides/melanotan-ii), which also acts strongly on brain receptors for appetite and sexual arousal. Melanotan I went on to become an approved medicine, while the melanotan II line led to the libido drug bremelanotide.

rows: Skin darkened in both poor and good tanners; none on placebo; peak 1-3 weeks after injections ended[^1]
Eumelanin in forearm skin roughly doubled one week after treatment[^5]
Melanin up 41% in those who burn easily; sunburn cells cut by over half and DNA damage markers by 59%[^2]

blocks.text: These were short, carefully supervised studies with pharmaceutical-grade drug. They do not tell us whether long-term cosmetic use is safe, or whether a drug-induced tan lowers skin cancer risk.

items: **Known effects of the molecule:** nausea, tiredness, dizziness and darkening of skin, freckles and moles, as recorded with the approved implant[^3]
**Mole changes:** dermatologists have reported new or changing moles, and a few melanomas, in people using unregulated melanotan products; a direct causal link has not been established[^4]
**Gray-market risks:** uncertain preparation and dosing, possible contamination, and infection from non-sterile mixing and injection[^4]
**Unknowns:** long-term effects, use in pregnancy, and effects in people with many moles or a melanoma history

blocks.text: The FDA has approved this molecule only as Scenesse, a 16 mg dissolving implant placed by a trained clinician, for adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria.[^3] No product is approved for cosmetic tanning, and selling injectable "melanotan" for human use is selling an unapproved drug. Several national health agencies have issued warnings about melanotan products.[^4]

Melanotan I is a real, well-studied molecule with a narrow medical use. Its tanning effect is genuine, but buying it online means injecting a product of unknown content without the monitoring that the approved implant requires, including regular skin checks. Sunless tanning lotions give a cosmetic tan without these risks.

evidence.label: Limited: small tanning trials, no long-term data
evidence.text: Randomized trials in healthy volunteers show the molecule reliably darkens skin and may reduce some UV damage markers,[^1][^2] and it has a regulatory-grade record as an approved drug for one disease.[^3] There is no controlled evidence on long-term cosmetic use or on gray-market products.

faq.q: Is Melanotan I the same as Scenesse?
faq.a: It is the same molecule. Scenesse is a manufactured, quality-controlled implant approved for one disease and given with skin monitoring, while online "Melanotan 1" is an unregulated powder.

faq.q: Is Melanotan I safer than Melanotan II?
faq.a: The molecule is more selective and has been studied far more, so it causes fewer brain-related effects such as spontaneous erections. That says little about the safety of an unregulated product of unknown content.[^4]

faq.q: Does it protect against skin cancer?
faq.a: That has never been shown. One trial found fewer sunburn cells and less UV-related DNA damage after treatment,[^2] but no study has measured skin cancer rates.
